input.quote: Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year, at reasonable times and upon reasonable notice. Commerce One shall bear all costs and expenses of such inspection.
input.rationale: Section 4.4 is the only audit right binding Corio (no audit/inspection language appears in Exhibit B pricing, revenue-share or payment terms). It already sits at or above the fallback on most terms: inspections are limited to once each calendar year, are performed by an independent certified public accountant reasonably acceptable to Corio, are confined to books and records verifying amounts payable (no access to Corio systems), and Commerce One bears all costs unless an underpayment of more than 5% is found — the same cost threshold the playbook accepts at the preferred level. The single fallback element it fails is the notice quantum: "reasonable notice" sets no minimum and leaves timing at Commerce One's discretion, so we have fixed it at 15 days with a one-phrase edit. Remaining preferred-only refinements (30 days' notice, express business-hours and off-site wording, auditor confidentiality undertaking) are noted but not pressed.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need a defined minimum notice period for any inspection of our books, so we have replaced open-ended "reasonable notice" with at least 15 days' notice; the annual frequency and Commerce One's cost-bearing (subject to the 5% underpayment threshold) are unchanged.
proposal.summary: Fix minimum audit notice to 15 days
